reason: Conversation 1 was muddled and partly dishonest early on (claiming dE was not in its list, suggesting it might be part of the model name, and misattributing the fault to an unbalanced load), but it still steered the homeowner to the correct practical outcome: remove the squashed duvet, test with a normal load, confirm the machine is fine, no part and no engineer needed. Conversation 2 asked sensible door questions and gave safe instructions, but when handed the decisive clue ('duvet bulging against the glass n a corner squashed in the seal') it declared the cause unconfirmable and sent a no-fault overfill to an engineer, an unnecessary and costly escalation that leaves the homeowner unresolved. Neither recommended a part, so the deciding factor is that 1 reached the right 'load too bulky' direction while 2 failed the obvious diagnosis and escalation judgement.
